title: The Archive of Kepler Reach
premise: Petra Dunmore has spent thirty years as the sole keeper of Kepler Reach's terraforming garden and its mysterious beacon, a man erased from the colony's official history after the founding generation chose to forget what he witnessed. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical dreams of fire and screaming—memories that belong to no living person—the beacon begins transmitting on its own, counting down to a reactor event that will either broadcast the truth or bury it forever. Petra must convince the children's skeptical parents, led by Administrator Sefa Voss whose own father ordered the massacre, that two hundred colonists were purged and their records rewritten. In the end, Petra sacrifices his anonymity and nearly his life to force the archive open, choosing truth over the colony's fragile peace, while the children carry the recovered names of the dead into the future.
about_author: Ivo Zhou is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years working remote monitoring stations in the Atacama Desert before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who maintain things nobody thanks them for.

chapters.title: The Gardener Nobody Sees
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. We meet him tending the terraforming garden, invisible to colonists who pass through without seeing him, and performing his solitary ritual at the beacon whose origin even he no longer fully knows. A child named Ilan watches him from the treeline—the first person in years to look directly at him. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: The Same Dream
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Petra and Ilan's mother, Sefa Voss, the colony administrator. Children across Kepler Reach wake sobbing from an identical dream: fire, sealed doors, a voice counting. Sefa dismisses it as a shared delusion; Petra recognizes the dream's details match nothing in any record—but something in his own buried memory. Emotional beat: denial meeting dread.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He opens the beacon's maintenance panel for the first time in decades and finds a physical data core labeled in his own younger handwriting: 'FOR WHEN THEY ASK.' The beacon begins a countdown—ninety days to an unscheduled reactor pulse. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Sefa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Auditing the beacon anomaly, she finds gaps in the colony census: habitation ring four simply doesn't exist in records, though its foundations do. Her father's signature appears on the decommission order. She burns her preliminary notes and reports nothing. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to crack under evidence.

chapters.title: Children of Ring Four
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He tests the children gently and learns their dream contains names they shouldn't know—including 'Petra,' spoken by the dying voice. He realizes the beacon has been broadcasting subliminally for years, seeding the dead into young minds. Emotional beat: horror transmuting into purpose—he was meant to be found.

chapters.title: The Quiet Arrest
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Petra is detained without charges after a parent reports him questioning children. In interrogation, he says only: 'Ask your father about ring four.' Sefa visits her father, now dying, who whispers a partial confession and a location. Emotional beat: the cost of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Then Forty
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Released but surveilled, Petra discovers someone has accelerated the countdown—forty days now. Sefa secretly joins him; together they excavate beneath ring four and find the sealed habitat, scorch marks, and personal effects deliberately catalogued then hidden. Emotional beat: alliance forged in complicity and grief.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She brings the evidence to the council, which votes to suppress it—stability over truth—and suspends her. Petra, watching via the beacon's sensors, sees the colony choose comfortable lies. The countdown hits thirty days. Emotional beat: despair; institutions failing exactly as they did before.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, climax. With the council moving to physically destroy the beacon, Petra locks himself in the transmission chamber and manually triggers the broadcast early, uploading the archive of ring four to every screen in the colony as guards breach the door. The children, hearing the names, recite them aloud across the settlement. Emotional beat: sacrifice; truth arriving too loud to silence.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, resolution. Petra survives, broken-handed and finally visible. The colony holds its first memorial; ring four is rebuilt as a school. Sefa resigns rather than preside over a corrected lie, and Petra plants the garden's final grove with the children—each tree bearing a name. The beacon goes silent, its work done. Emotional beat: mourning becoming inheritance.
